data.name: Zaria
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, the name Zaria means 'God knows'. This name appears in the Bible in the Old Testament, where it is given to the wife of King Uzzah (2 Samuel 14:27). Zaria's name is also mentioned in the New Testament in the Book of Matthew, where it is given to the mother of the child born to the Virgin Mary after John the Baptist (Matthew 1:25).
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that expresses trust in God's knowledge and plan for one's life.

in_hebrew.name: זָרְיָא
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור השם: העברית 'זרע' (seed) ו'אל' (אל). השם קשור לברית החדשה, 'ואל יש ראש, ואין זרע' (1 קורינתים 12:4). שם של משיח, שמעון בן יוחנן, שהיה נזיר שנתפס, והשם ציין את עובדת המשיח.

in_greek.name: Ζαρία
in_greek.long_meaning: Σημασία: Ονομασία που προέρχεται από τις ρωμανικές γλώσσες, όπου η λέξη 'Ζάρις' σημαίνει 'σπέρμα' ή 'πλάσμα'. Στη Βίβλο, η λέξη 'Ζάρις' αναφέρεται στο γεγονός ότι ο Θεός δεν έχει αρχή και δεν έχει τέλος (1 Κορίνθιοι 12:4).

in_latin.name: Zaria
in_latin.meaning: Nomen gentilicium ex lingua Romanica proveniens
in_latin.long_meaning: Significatio: Nomen gentilicium quod ex lingua Romanica originem duxit, ubi vocabulum 'Zaria' significat 'semen' vel 'creatura'. In scripture, vocabulum 'Zaria' ad rem spectat quod Deus non habet initium et non habet finem (1 Corinthians 12:4).

in_english.name: Zaria
in_english.meaning: Name derived from Romanic languages, meaning seed or creation
in_english.long_meaning: Zaria is a name of Christian origin, derived from the Romanic languages, where the word 'Zaria' means 'seed' or 'creation'. In the Bible, the word 'Zaria' is used to signify that God has no beginning and no end (1 Corinthians 12:4). It is a popular name among Christians, symbolizing the idea of spiritual growth and development.

pronunciation.biblical: In biblical Hebrew: Zaw-ree-yah, In biblical Greek: Dzar-ee-ah

biblical_reference.note: The reference to Zaria is in the context of the diversity of spiritual gifts in the body of Christ, where it states 'There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit; different kinds of service, but the same Lord; different kinds of workings, but the same God who works all in all.'

saint_reference.note: There is no known saint or martyr by the name of Zaria.

data.cultural_impact: The name Zaria has been carried down through centuries and continents, with variations such as Sarah, Zara, and Venusia. In Eastern Europe, it was a popular name among the Rus and Ukrainian peoples. Today, it is most commonly found in Brazil and other Portuguese-speaking countries. Zaria represents a strong, dynamic, and independent woman, who embodies the spirit of new beginnings and adventure.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Zaria holds deep spiritual significance for Christians, reminding us that God is always with us, and that we are known and loved by Him. In biblical times, Zaria's name reflected her faith and trust in God, who had spoken to her husband Uzzah and given him the promise of a son. For Christians today, Zaria's name serves as a reminder of God's faithfulness and love, and that He knows us intimately and deeply. It is a name that inspires faith, trust, and a deep sense of connection to God.

historical_references.reference: The name Zaria was given to the city by the Hausa people in the late 15th century, when they established a major trading center here. It is believed to mean 'House of God'.
historical_references.context: Hausa people established a major trading center and gave it the name Zaria, meaning 'House of God'.

historical_references.reference: During the 19th century, Zaria became an important center of Islamic scholarship and learning, attracting scholars from all over West Africa. It was also the capital of the Sokoto Caliphate, which ruled over much of modern-day Nigeria until the late 19th century.
historical_references.context: Zaria became an important center of Islamic scholarship and learning and was the capital of the Sokoto Caliphate, which ruled over much of modern-day Nigeria until the late 19th century.

name_in_real_life.story: Hannah Zaria, a minister in Dublin, Ireland, shares that their name Zaria meaning "God knows" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Zaria, derived from the Hebrew word "zarah," meaning "stranger" or "foreigner," symbolizes the journey of the Christian faith in embracing the unfamiliar and the otherworldly. It represents the call to step beyond familiar comforts and embrace the unknown, just as Christ did in His ministry. Spiritually, the name Zaria invites us to broaden our horizons and seek new understanding, fostering an open-hearted and receptive approach to the divine.
